<thought>From the isotopic pattern, the clear M+1 peak (~6.7% of M) indicates the presence of carbon (13C). The noticeable M+2 peak (~6.7% of M) is consistent with the natural abundance of 34S (≈4%) combined with carbon contributions, indicating sulfur. No other element shows a distinctive isotopic signature at these intensities. Therefore, the definitively identifiable elements are carbon and sulfur.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'S']</final_answer>
